chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
For everything to which people say 'how good!', there is an evil hidden in this world.

key_terms.الدَّهْرُ: Time / The world / Eternity (often personified as the agent of hidden trials)
key_terms.يَوْمَ سَوْءٍ: A day of evil / A time of hardship

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean by 'there is an evil hidden in this world'?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) teaches that for every apparent good thing to which people exclaim 'how good!', there is a hidden evil or difficulty concealed by time (al-dahr). This highlights the transient nature of worldly blessings and the inevitability of trials, reflecting the Shia concept of *taqiyya* of fate where outward prosperity often masks inner spiritual decay or impending hardship. The saying serves as a warning against complacency in worldly success, urging believers to look beyond superficial appearances to the deeper realities of divine decree.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 286. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
For everything to which people say “how good!” there is an evil hidden in this world.
